coordinate_space: All placements, support points, occupancy and triggers are logical; drawing details and contours are artwork pixels.

design_brief.identity: Inhabited timber-and-plaster village rooms, with an industrial watermill and a two-storey travellers' inn.
design_brief.intention: Recognizable work, household care and hospitality, without inventing occupations or new lore.
design_brief.materials: Retained warm oak floor/plaster shell and furnishings; new restrained oak, iron, stone, canvas and woven-linen details at native 2x.
design_brief.scope: Fifteen retained interiors across thirteen buildings, plus exactly one inn guest floor. No regional changes, new stock, rewards, prices or recovery systems.
design_brief.canon: Existing residents, quest props and services retain ownership. Decoration is not a collectible or new occupation.

mill_processing.work_access: Sorting table [264,180] and entrance [252,294] retained. Millstone is north of the table; western and southern handling aisle stays clear.

stairs.meaning: A directional transfer at the first tread. Arrival is on the clear southern landing. Both stair doors stay disarmed until the player leaves the stair/landing rectangle, including Continue.

guest_floor.circulation: Four sleeping bays correspond to the four exterior guest-storey window bays. Timber screens end at y198, leaving the common corridor and east stair clear. No upper rest_profile, service, keeper, inventory or quest.

old_save_policy: No migration or version change. Existing Game.begin_journey retains exact valid positions; positions now overlapping the explicitly named mill base/stair stringers use its existing checked room-entry fallback. Quest, party, inventory, gold and actor ownership are not mutated by the art extension.

owned_lantern_surface.replacement_policy: Retain canonical registered phase art at explicit compatibility 2x; replace generic-paper aliases, not ownership, state keys, timing or credits. Preserve upstream #250 zero-alpha collected contents; the separately owned real table stays visible at its full original footprint, without a second frame or table overlay.
